steps.caption: Herald decides what may interrupt you
Five messages land at the same moment
The 3D character in the corner says one
Four wait, each with the reason
Next comes the most important one
The last two collapse into one line

posts.text:
Send Herald five messages at once. It says one, holds four, then says the two that matter most and folds the last two into a single line: 2 more messages waiting.

Each hold comes with its reason (delivering-another), and nothing is dropped.

Herald is how a message gets delivered in person: a 3D character walks into the corner of your page and tells you, with a link to the thing it is about. An interruption only works while it is rare, so the budget ships with it: an importance floor, a rate limit, quiet hours, dedupe.

The reel is the real library running in a browser tab, on its default body: auto, the avatar first, then a card when the page has no GPU.

Change the rules, send your own message, and watch what the engine decides: three.ws/herald

A message can come from anything that can make an HTTPS request: a build script, a terminal, an agent over MCP.

It is always delivered to the caller's own sessions, so a key can never be used to interrupt somebody else.
